definitions.window: The last three completed regular-season weeks ending at the cutoff, the same calendar weeks for every player (recent form's Last 3). The baseline is every earlier week.
definitions.appearance: A week with a stats row or an offensive snap. A bye (B) and a game his team played without him (D) are not games and are never zeros.
definitions.opportunity: Targets for a receiver or tight end; carries plus targets for a running back. A team share pools his total over his team's total in the games he played.
definitions.ceiling: P90 of the weekly start/sit model's distribution of his points given that he plays: one week in ten at or above it. Not a 90% chance of a big game, and not a ranking of boom probabilities.
definitions.typical_week: The weekly model's own account of the same player in a typical week (his team's average lines, half at home, equal rest, a league-average defense). The difference is the matchup's modelled effect, counted once.
definitions.espn_rostered: ESPN's public share of ESPN leagues rostering him. It describes ESPN leagues, not yours; an unknown reading is not 0%.
definitions.pace: Points per game × 17: arithmetic extrapolation, not a projection.
definitions.snap_share: His share of his team's offensive snaps. Teammates share the field, so snap shares overlap and never add to 100%.
definitions.red_zone: Carries and targets on plays snapped at the opponent's 20 or closer (inside the five: the 5 or closer), counted from nflverse play-by-play.

limitations: Stories describe completed weeks and the published weekly distribution; none is a forecast of a result, and none says a player is due.
No expected-points estimate is published (ADR-086), so a gap between workload and scoring is described, never quantified as luck.
Snaps are not routes and a target is not a first read: no route, route-tree or coverage claim is made.
ESPN roster share describes ESPN leagues; a low share does not mean a player is available in your league.
League size changes nothing here: no story reads a replacement level or a VORP.
